AccessibilityGuide.Description: Just turn on this one switch in System Settings.
AccessibilityGuide.DescriptionAfter: This window changes on its own once it’s on.
AccessibilityGuide.Title: Turn on access for Split
AccessibilityGuide.GrantedDescription: You can now move windows with shortcuts.
AccessibilityGuide.GrantedTry: Bring any window to the front and press:
AlertInformativeTextRestoreDefaults: Shortcuts you changed will go back to how Split came.
AlertInformativeTextRunningInBackground: Shortcuts keep working. To open settings again, open Split from the Applications folder.
AlertInformativeTextRunningInBackgroundW: Shortcuts keep working. To open settings again, open Split from the Start menu.
AlertInformativeTextRunningInBackgroundL: Shortcuts keep working. To open settings again, open Split from your app list.
AlertInformativeTextShortcutAlreadyInUse: Another Split action uses %@. Choose a different shortcut.
AlertInformativeTextSystemWideShortcutAl: macOS already uses %@. Choose a different shortcut, or change it in System Settings › Keyboard › Keyboard Shortcuts.
AlertMessageTextRunningInBackground: Hide Split from the menu bar?
AlertMessageTextRunningInBackgroundWin: Hide Split from the notification area?
AlertMessageTextRunningInBackgroundLinux: Hide Split from the system tray?
ApplicationRefusedAccess: %1$@ refused to let Split move its windows. Quit %1$@ and open it again.
AutoUpdateHint: Split looks for a new version once a day and asks before installing it.
ConflictingWindowApps: %@ is running and may use the same shortcuts as Split. If windows land in the wrong size, change one app’s shortcuts or quit it.
DisplayChangeHint: Windows from an unplugged monitor move to the screens left; plug it back in and they go back.
DisplayRearranged: Monitors changed, so %ld windows were rearranged
DisplayRearranged|one: Monitors changed, so %ld window was rearranged
DisplayRestored: %ld windows went back to their places
DisplayRestored|one: %ld window went back to its place
FeedbackColorHint: The preview in the menu uses this color too.
FeedbackShortcutHint: The shortcut and action name appear on screen.
FeedbackTryHint: Changes play around this window right away.
LaunchAtLoginHint: Split starts by itself when you log in to this Mac.
LaunchAtLoginHintWin: Split starts by itself when you log in to this computer.
LaunchAtLoginHintLinux: Split starts by itself when you log in to this computer.
LayoutSaveAuto: Load automatically when these displays are connected
LayoutSaveMessage: Saves where the visible windows are under a name. Click it in the menu to bring them all back at once.
LayoutSaveOpenApps: Also open apps that are closed
LayoutSavedEmpty: None yet. Make one with “Save Current Layout…” below.
Migration.LegacyRunningBody: Split and Spectacle both react to the same shortcuts, so windows end up in the wrong size. Quit Spectacle and remove it from your login items?
MoveFeedbackHint: Shows briefly after a window moves.
PermissionOffHint: Off. Windows can't move until you turn it on.
ProFeatures: Put each app's windows in a place you choose, open a whole workspace at once, split the screen into your own grid, and keep settings the same on all your Macs
ProFeaturesWin: Put each app's windows in a place you choose, open a whole workspace at once, split the screen into your own grid, and keep settings the same on all your computers
ProFeaturesLinux: Put each app's windows in a place you choose, open a whole workspace at once, split the screen into your own grid, and keep settings the same on all your computers
ProFreeUntilLaunch: Free to use until Pro launches
SectionArrangeHint: Places up to 9 visible windows on the current screen at once: 1 full, 2 side by side, 3 one big and two stacked, 4 a grid. Undo puts them all back.
SectionThirdsHint: Press again to go to the next third.
ShortcutSheetHoldWin: Hold Alt+Win for the shortcut list
ShortcutSheetHoldLinux: Hold Alt+Super for the shortcut list
ShortcutSheetHoldHint: Hold ⌥⌘ for a second to see every shortcut.
ShortcutSheetHoldHintWin: Hold Alt+Win for a second to see every shortcut.
ShortcutSheetHoldHintLinux: Hold Alt+Super for a second to see every shortcut.
ShortcutsHint: Click a shortcut to change it, or × to clear it.
ShortcutsNotRegistered: Another app already uses these shortcuts: %@
ShowMenuBarIconHint: When off, open Split from the Applications folder to get back to these settings.
ShowMenuBarIconHintWin: When off, open Split from the Start menu to get back to these settings.
ShowMenuBarIconHintLinux: When off, open Split from your app list to get back to these settings.
SpacesReorderHint: The macOS setting "Automatically rearrange Spaces based on most recent use" is on. Turn it off to keep the order.
SpacesSeparate: More desktops after unplugging a monitor?
SpacesSeparateHint: Turning off "Displays have separate Spaces" makes one set of desktops for all monitors. You need to log out after changing it.
TipArrange: Tip: %@ arranges every visible window at once
TipFullscreenAgain: Tip: press again to go back to the old size
TipSheet: Tip: hold ⌥⌘ for a second to see all shortcuts
TipSheetWin: Tip: hold Alt+Win for a second to see all shortcuts
TipSheetLinux: Tip: hold Alt+Super for a second to see all shortcuts
UpdateAvailableBody: Install Split %@? Split will restart after installing.
WindowGapHint: Leaves room between windows. Screen edges stay flush.
AccountSignInLine: Sign In with Your RUNNERS Account
PhoneHint: Sign in with your RUNNERS account to arrange this computer's windows from the Split phone app.
PhoneSignInWrong: The email or password is wrong.
PhoneSignInFailed: Could not sign in. Check the internet connection and try again.
PhoneConnected: Connected. The phone app can reach this computer.
